entries.title: Deuteronomy 22:1
segments: Hide thyself from them; pass by as if you did not see them; refuse to care for them.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 22:2
segments: The Old Testament as well as the New requires men to do to others as in like circumstances they ought to wish others to do to them.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 22:3
segments: Things which others have lost, and which we find, are not ours if by using suitable means we can find the owner.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 22:4
segments: The law of God requires us to exercise compassion not only towards our fellow men, but also towards animals in distress, and to make all proper efforts to relieve them.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 22:5
segments:
Shall not wear that; because it tended to impurity and wickedness. 
 
All practices which tend to impurity of heart of or life, in ourselves or others, should be avoided.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 22:6
segments:
Shalt not take the dam; it would be cruel, and tend to sanction cruelty, and also to extirpate that species of birds. 
 
The directions of God are suited to lessen, and should they be perfectly followed, to do away the selfishness and cruelty of the human heart, and lead it to delight in the happiness of the whole sensitive creation.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 22:7
segments:
Take the young; that is, the young only: not a command to take young birds from the nest, but a prohibition of their being taken with the parent bird. 
 
  Prolong thy days; by showing a tender and kind spirit, even to the brute creation. 
 
The manifestaton of a kind and compassionate disposition is favorable to the continuance of life, prosperity, and happiness.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 22:8
segments:
A battlement for thy roof; a wall or railing around the roof, to keep persons from falling off; as their roofs were flat, and were often resorted to for air and exercise. 
 
Carelessness as well as cruelty is offensive to God, and tends to bring numerous evils upon men.  If others suffer through our neglect, we shall be held responsible at the divine tribunal.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 22:9
segments:
vv 9-12. 
 
  Divers sorts; these directions may have been designed to prevent the Israelites from imitating the heathen, and keep them a separate people.  Some think that they have also a symbolical meaning, and forbid the mixture of things that are incongruous in morals and religion.  Compare

. 
 
Jehovah delights in harmony, propriety, decency, and order.  Every thing contrary to these, and tending to corrupt the imagination, pervert the judgment, or deprave the heart, is offensive in his sight.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 22:13
segments:
vv 13-21. 
 
  Occasions of speech against her; these directions were designed to prevent unjust accusations, to protect the innocent, and punish the guilty.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 22:21
segments: Marriage is an institution of God, established at the creation, and to continue to the end of time.  Its obligations are most sacred, and those who violate them are exposed to his awful curse.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 22:22
segments: They shall both of them die; this was on the ground that both were consenting to the wickedness.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 22:25
segments: By the penalty which God under the Jewish dispensation affixed to adultery, he showed his deep and unchanging abhorrence of that crime, and the sore punishment which, without repentance awaits the guilty in the future world.
